A differential equation of the form \displaystyle\displaystyle\frac{{\rm d}y}{{\rm d}x}=f(x) is known as a directly integrable ODE. Technically it is a kind of separable ODE. It can be solved by integration. Solve the following directly integrable differential equations : (a)​ \displaystyle\displaystyle\frac{{\rm d}y}{{\rm d}x}=2x (b)​ \displaystyle\displaystyle\frac{{\rm d}z}{{\rm d}t}=t\sin t (c)​ \displaystyle\displaystyle\frac{{\rm d}u}{{\rm d}x}=x^{3} subject to u=5 at x=0 . Short answer (a) x^{2}+C , (b) -t\cos t+\sin t+C , (c) \frac{x^{4}}{4}+5 13. Solve the differential equation \displaystyle(x^{2}+3)\displaystyle\frac{{\rm d}y}{{\rm d}x}=4x .
